correctness.rationale: Substitution of e1∘e1=2e1, e1∘e2=e2, e2²=0 into R(x)∘R(y)=R(R(x)∘y+x∘R(y)) gives equations 2(a²+bc)=0, 2c(a+d)=0, b(a+d)=0, bc+d²=0. For char≠2 they reduce to d=-a and a²+bc=0, exactly R²=0. Every automorphism is P(t,s)=[[1,0],[t,s]], s≠0; direct conjugation sends b→b/s. If b≠0 normalizes to U, if b=0≠R then to L, with zero separate. In characteristic two the b≠0 branch again normalizes to U, b=0,d=0 gives 0,L, and scalar-invariant D_a (a≠0), and no others. Over finite q, counts q² odd and 2q²−q even, orbit types respectively three and q+2. Independent direct basis-law and conjugation enumeration over GF2, GF4, GF3 and GF5 corroborated all counts; arbitrary-field proof is symbolic, not prime-field extrapolation.

value.rationale: Moduli of a fixed low-dimensional Jordan algebra under its actual automorphism group are natural classification objects; the positive-characteristic bifurcation introduces an entirely new one-parameter family of semisimple solutions and changes orbit count from constant three to q+2. The exact variety equations and orbit sizes enable finite-field moduli comparison and explain why a complex parametrization is not a field-uniform classification. This is a structural characteristic jump, not a mere rebranding of known matrices.
residual_risks: Only this Jordan type and weight zero, not all 2D Jordan operator moduli.

limitations: The characteristic-two algebra is the fixed multiplication table after base change, not an identification of classification labels over C.
Counts hold for every prime power q, using symbolic proof; finite-field tests sample only q=2,3,4,5.
